name: Lactose intolerance
surveyQuestion: Do you have any of these health conditions? (select all that apply) -> Lactose intolerance. Check question: Has a doctor or a breath test told you that you cannot digest lactose, or do milk, curd or sweets reliably cause bloating, gas, cramps or loose stools within about 30 minutes to 2 hours? Yes, diagnosed / Yes, I think so (lifestyle-only mode) / No / Not sure. Safety question: Is this for a baby or child under 18, or do you get hives, swelling, wheeze, vomiting or blood in stool after milk? (Yes: no targets set, see a doctor)

targets.source: ICMR-NIN 2020 (secondary, unverified); no lactose-specific change found
NIH consensus (Suchy 2010); AHRQ review (Wilt 2010); Shaukat 2010 (via search)
AHRQ evidence report 192 (via NIH consensus summary)
Topic 30; no lactose-specific fluid value found

bloodMarkers.marker: Hydrogen breath test after 25 g lactose (diagnostic; doctor-ordered)
bloodMarkers.target: A rise of 20 ppm or more above baseline is positive for lactose malabsorption; symptoms during the test are recorded
bloodMarkers.source: Rezaie et al., North American Consensus 2017 (via search)

bloodMarkers.marker: Calcium intake (diet, not a blood test)
bloodMarkers.target: 1,000 mg/day (1,200 for 60+); blood calcium is kept in range by bone so it does not show a low intake
Doctor-set; no lactose-specific target; stored only (see P12)
Stored only; unexplained anaemia is a red flag

bloodMarkers.marker: Total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides, HbA1c, uric acid, eGFR, TSH

waterMl.notes: No change from the general FitPlate range (topic 30: 2,500 ml men, 2,000 ml women). Lactose intolerance does not call for more or less water. During a bout of diarrhoea keep drinking normally (ORS from a pharmacist if advised) and see a doctor if it lasts more than a few days or there is blood. Milk, curd and chaas count as fluid but may bring symptoms; use water, nimbu pani without added sugar, or lactose-free options. With kidney, heart or liver disease, pregnancy, a fluid limit or a diuretic show the general range only. Follow your doctor's advice.

foodsFavour: live-culture dahi/curd and thick strained curd in small portions (often better tolerated than milk)
paneer (low lactose, est. 1-3 g per 100 g)
ghee in normal cooking amounts (near zero lactose)
hard aged cheese in small amounts
ragi, sesame (til) and almonds for calcium
methi, drumstick leaves and curry leaves (low-oxalate greens)
calcium-set tofu and fortified soy milk or other fortified plant milks (unsweetened, check calcium on label)
small fish eaten with bones (sardine, anchovy)
dal, eggs, fish, poultry, soy and nuts for protein, B12 and riboflavin
foodsLimit: large single servings of milk (more than about 1 cup / 250 ml at once) on an empty stomach
kheer, rabri, basundi, gajar halwa, milk-based mithai (khoa/mawa, peda, barfi, gulab jamun)
milk-heavy drinks (cold coffee, milkshake, sweet lassi, several cups of milk chai)
cream and khoa-based gravies (malai kofta, shahi paneer, navratan korma)
milk powder (SMP), whey and milk-solids in packaged foods when they trigger symptoms
processed cheese spreads and cheese slices in large amounts (est.)

conflictsWith.rule: Lactose is one FODMAP; do one change at a time with a diary so symptoms are not blamed on lactose alone (P16). Do not remove dairy and wheat together without a doctor or dietitian
Untreated celiac disease can cause secondary lactose intolerance that fades as the gut heals; test before dropping gluten; lactose limit may be temporary (P19; doctor-led)
Calcium target 1,000-1,200 mg must be met without dairy; the higher calcium need overrides; doctor sets any supplement (P20)
Dairy cuts can lower B12 and calcium intake; use the stricter of the two profiles' reminders; supplements are doctor-led (P12)
Vegan already excludes dairy; P18 adds nothing but the hidden-lactose label check; P34 rules for calcium, B12, iodine apply
If calcium-rich foods or supplements are used to replace dairy, stone-formers keep calcium from food and avoid high-oxalate greens (P14); doctor decides
Replacing milk with nuts, tofu or fortified plant milks changes potassium and phosphorus; P13 rules override and the doctor sets the plan

warnings: General information, not medical advice; FitPlate does not diagnose lactose intolerance.
Infants and children under 18: no targets set; see a paediatrician (milk allergy is different and can be dangerous).
Hives, lip or face swelling, wheeze, repeated vomiting or blood in stool after milk: possible milk allergy, seek care now.
Blood in stool, unexplained weight loss, persistent diarrhoea, night-time symptoms, anaemia, fever or severe pain: doctor first, do not assume lactose.
Do not stop all dairy for months without a calcium, vitamin D, protein and B12 plan.
Lactase enzyme tablets or drops, probiotics and calcium or vitamin D supplements: the doctor or pharmacist decides; no dose is given by the app.
Pregnancy and breastfeeding: the doctor sets calcium and any supplements (P22, P23).
